panels.description: Wide, full page width. A new star-fort bastion of laterite and packed earth jutting from the fort wall like an angled tooth, seen from below and to one side. Dry-season light, red dust hanging in the air. On its point, two small figures under a banner staff: the royal standard, red with a silver conch, at the top; below it a smaller pennant, white with a dark blue diagonal line crossed by a dark blue curved line.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: By the first dry season after Kollamkara's valley, the fort had a name for the new bastion.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The foreigner's tooth. Half in jest, half in grudging respect.

panels.description: From the bastion, looking down on the drill ground. Maravar horse in their own cloth (white mundu hitched, short cotton jackets, red shoulder cloths) wheeling in pairs between marked posts along the base of the wall. Behind them a rank of Nair musketeers in white mundu hitched at the knee, bare-chested or in short cotton jackets, firing a controlled volley over the horses' backs at wooden targets in the scrub. No uniforms, no coats. A small field gun recoiling on well-braced wheels, white smoke rolling.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A drill that would have made my younger self, and De Lannoy's old company captains, splutter.

panels.description: On the bastion. De Lannoy: tall, pale hair, bare-headed, a worn white Travancore coat patched at the elbows, shading his eyes with one hand. Nagoji beside him, arms folded, NOT yet in uniform: Kerala topknot, no turban, white mundu with shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no sash, no bandages, no knife; first grey at the temples, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: They are improving.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You sound almost pleased.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Almost.

panels.description: Low angle up the staff. At the top, the royal standard, red with a silver conch. Beneath it, a smaller pennant, white with a dark blue diagonal line crossed by a dark blue curved line. Both snapping in the wind against a hard blue sky.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A line for the wall. A curve for the horse. He had drawn it himself.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: If you insist on naming bastions after me, I insist on at least choosing a decent symbol.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The two men from behind, looking out over the drill, the point of the tooth aimed outward at the scrub and the hills. Nagoji's black topknot and bare shoulders under the shoulder cloth, the silver chain glinting; De Lannoy taller beside him in his white coat.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Better a tooth than a sore. At least this one bites outward.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not everyone liked how sharp that bite was becoming.

panels.description: The palace hall. Chiefs and officers seated along the walls, most with sandal-paste or ash marks on their foreheads. A heavy older Nair chief with ash stripes on his forehead leaning toward his neighbour, deliberately loud, eyes sliding to the far end of the hall where Nagoji and De Lannoy stand together. Nagoji not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no bandages, no knife); De Lannoy in his white coat.

copy.speaker: NAIR CHIEF
copy.text: The Deccan rider and the Dutch captain.

copy.speaker: NAIR CHIEF
copy.text: Two foreigners teaching us how to use our own land.

panels.description: Padmini Amma (in her fifties, thick black hair coiled at the nape and beginning to grey, simple gold, cotton sari, long walking stick) turning her head toward him, unhurried.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Teaching us how to keep it.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If you prefer to learn from men who have never seen a European musket up close, that is your choice. Do not complain when your sons bleed for it.

panels.description: Evening. The long rampart walk. Nagoji (not yet in uniform: topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no bandages, no knife) and De Lannoy side by side. Below them on the drill ground, a ragged line of Nair musketeers in white mundu, no uniforms, with gaps where men should be standing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Still, the resentment was there.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: We must not become a separate standard. If they see us as a force within a force, we will be cut out like a tumour when the monarchy changes.

panels.description: Lannoy shrugging, eyes on the palace roofs below. Nagoji watching him sidelong.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You think that will happen?

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: In my land, kings fall. In yours, too.

panels.description: Full width. The palace roofline spread below the rampart in the dusk, tiled roofs stepping down toward the audience hall where the throne platform stands. The two men small on the rampart above it, Lannoy beginning to laugh.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We fight for the structure, then. Not the man.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: We fight so that whoever sits on that platform cannot easily undo what we have built. It is a selfish defence, in a way.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Selfish defence keeps people alive.

panels.description: A map table. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and stylus) standing between Nagoji and De Lannoy, who lean on the table from opposite sides over a plan of a wall. Nagoji not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat); De Lannoy in his white coat.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Stone where you must. Earth where you can.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You spend as much time keeping us from killing each other as keeping the king alive.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: It is all the same work. Preventable deaths exhaust me.

panels.description: A hot afternoon, combined drill. A young Nair musketeer, barely more than a boy, in a white mundu hitched at the knee, bare-chested, no uniform, has fired too early: smoke at his muzzle, a spurt of dust far wide of the wooden target. De Lannoy striding toward him.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Again.

panels.description: The youth fumbling at his powder horn, hands shaking. Behind him Nagoji trots past on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat, mundu hitched for the saddle, turning to call down. Nagoji not yet in uniform: topknot, shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Breathe. The gun does not fear your heartbeat.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Make it go slower than the drum.

panels.description: Later, wide. The same recruit in a line of Nair musketeers in white mundu, no uniforms, firing in perfect time, muzzles angled high over a pair of Maravar riders cantering past below. De Lannoy (white coat) and Nagoji (topknot, white mundu, no coat) at the edge of the frame, both nodding.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Good.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Now do it when someone is shouting in your ear.

panels.description: The boy grinning, sweat running into his eyes, musket grounded.

copy.speaker: RECRUIT
copy.text: Yes, Kappittan. Yes, Pillai.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He did not care which of us got which title.

panels.description: Evening on a lamplit verandah. Ibrahim Marakkar (short coat over a vest with bulging pockets, scar from the left ear to the jaw) with a cup of toddy. Padmini beside him, her stick across her knees. Nagoji listening, not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no bandages, no knife).

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The Dutch are no longer the only storm. There are new flags at the northern ports.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: We will need more than one tooth. And more than one kind of jaw.

panels.description: Velinadu, a courtyard in daylight. Revathi Bayi (deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline, a tali at her throat, first grey threading her hair) seated at a low table beside an old steward, going through a bundle of palm-leaf accounts, a brass grain measure at her elbow. She does not look up. Nagoji standing before her, not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat).

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You and De Lannoy are useful.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are also convenient scapegoats.

panels.description: Revathi handing a palm leaf back to the steward without looking at it; her eyes are on Nagoji now. Nagoji, one eyebrow up.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Scapegoats?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If the army fails, they will say the foreigner misled it. If it grows too strong, they will say the foreigner twisted it.

panels.description: Wide. Revathi has risen and the steward is going. Her gaze has drifted past Nagoji and out through the open courtyard gate to the south, where far off, small and grey above the palms, stands the angled point of the fort's new bastion.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: If a wall ever falls, I would rather it land on the Dutchman who designed it than on my people.

panels.description: Two-shot. Her hand rests flat on the stack of palm leaves. She is not smiling.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You make the future sound bleak.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I make it sound like what it often is.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Complicated.

panels.description: Wide. The war hall at night, lamplit, maps pinned to the walls. A dozen officers in their own clothes, no uniforms: Nair captains, older and heavier men with sandal-paste or ash marks on their foreheads; Maravar commanders with red shoulder cloths; a few men of the hired Madurai regiment in turbans. Nagoji among them, nearest the camera and lit: not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, no coat), the only officer with a silver chain of office and no forehead mark, small gold ear stud, first grey at the temples. De Lannoy apart, near the maps, in his white coat, his face carefully blank. At the head of the table, Marthanda Varma (V13 varma-v1 face, cream and gold, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, gold necklaces) holding up a coat like a trophy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The king's next demand made Revathi's complications feel almost simple.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This is what my army will wear.

panels.description: Insert, tight on the table as the uniform is laid out: a long white cotton coat of European cut with a column of plain, undecorated brass buttons catching the lamplight, a red waistcoat, knee breeches, stockings, buckled shoes.
directions: No text. Let the buttons shine.

panels.description: Varma, one hand flat on the coat.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The drill is European. The muskets are European. The forts are built to European designs.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: It is time the men who use these things look as if they belong to the same army.

panels.description: An older Nair captain, heavy and grey, ash stripes on his forehead, shifting his weight, careful.

copy.speaker: NAIR CAPTAIN
copy.text: Maharaja, our men have always worn...

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: What they pleased.

panels.description: Full width. Varma leaning over the table toward the room, the white coat under his hands.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: When a Dutch officer looks through his glass at my lines, I want him to see something that makes his stomach turn.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Not a rabble. A machine.

panels.description: Varma turning toward De Lannoy at the maps.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have seen European armies. Tell them.

panels.description: De Lannoy stepping forward to the table, the room's eyes on him.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: In Europe, when regiments dress alike, they move alike.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: When an enemy sees a line of men dressed the same, he sees not individuals but a wall. Walls are harder to break than crowds.

panels.description: Varma.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And when those walls wear coats like his own army's, the enemy hesitates. He wonders if his maps are wrong.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Hesitation kills.

panels.description: Nagoji among the officers, nearest the camera, looking at the coat on the table: not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no bandages, no knife), no forehead mark. At the edges of the frame the other officers, older men with forehead marks, nod. He does not.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The logic was sound.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But I did not see logic.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Bleeding in from the panel edge like a stain, not a clean flashback frame: a stone corridor in Goa, slick with monsoon damp. Far down the corridor, two Portuguese soldiers in long white coats with red cuffs and red waistcoats, black tricornes, walking away (white-dominant, not redcoats). Nearer, the Goa officer: a pale European, clean-shaven pale jaw, hair tied in a queue under a black tricorne, a deep-cuffed white coat edged with gilt lace, ornate gilt buttons, a red waistcoat, a smallsword at his hip; the frame cuts off at his chin and his eyes are never shown; he is adjusting one cuff. Behind him, two Portuguese gaol guards (dented steel morion helmets, loose off-white shirts, buff leather jerkins, dark breeches; nothing red or blue) dragging two chained prisoners: Keshavrao (about nineteen, beardless apart from a faint youthful moustache, narrow shoulders, black hair hacked short, faded grey-brown torn tunic) and, seen from behind, Nagoji in his captivity rags (torn ochre sleeveless tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged hands, ankle irons, barefoot, long curly hair loose). The guards' buckled shoes on wet stone.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I saw Goa.

panels.description: Back in the hall, the stain fading at the panel edge. Tight on Nagoji's throat and jaw: clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, the silver chain at his collarbone, the edge of his shoulder cloth. No coat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The coat was not Portuguese. The cut was different, the buttons plain rather than ornate.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But the colour, the shape, the entire idea of wrapping myself in European cloth...

panels.description: Varma across the table, his eyes on Nagoji.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have concerns, Pillai.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not a question.

panels.description: Two-shot across the table, the white coat lying between them. Nagoji answering, level: not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat). Varma listening.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have served you in my own clothes. They have not prevented me from drilling your horse.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: No. But your horse are a small part of this army. When the full force marches, I want one face. Not many.

panels.description: Over Nagoji's shoulder onto Varma, the coat's plain brass buttons in the foreground.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The men will resist. They will see this as...

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Foreign. Yes. As they saw muskets once. As they saw star forts.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They learned. So will you.

panels.description: Wide. Varma addressing the room. The officers, men with forehead marks, already turning for the door. Nagoji not moving, the only man with a silver chain of office and no forehead mark.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Coats will be issued within the month. Officers will set the example.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Dismissed.

panels.description: The emptied hall. Only the two of them and the lamps. Varma not looking up from the coat. Nagoji not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no bandages, no knife).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You are thinking of Goa.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am thinking of many things.

panels.description: Varma lifting the coat, holding it at arm's length.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You are thinking that this coat looks like the coat of the men who broke your fingers and chained you in a ship's hold.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: It is not the same coat. The men who wear it will not be the same men.

panels.description: Nagoji's hand, ridged fingernails, the old brand at the inner left wrist, stopped a finger's width above one plain brass button of the coat. His face above it, out of focus.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Knowing and feeling are different animals.

panels.description: Varma setting the coat down on the table between them.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Yes. They are. But I do not have time to wait for your feelings to catch up with your knowledge.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Other Europeans will come. When they do, I want them to see an army that they recognise and fear.

panels.description: Full width. Varma at the window, his back to the room, night outside. Nagoji alone at the table with the white coat.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Talk to De Lannoy. He wears the coat already.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ask him how it sits on a man who once wore a different one.

panels.description: Wide. The foreigner's tooth at sunset, the training ground below painted copper and dust, the evening drill underway (men in white mundu, no coats yet). De Lannoy at the parapet with a cup of toddy, not turning. Nagoji climbing the last steps, not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat, no bandages, no knife).

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: You stayed behind. I assume you did not simply want to admire the buttons.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The king told me to speak with you. About wearing the coat.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Ah.

panels.description: Low angle along the parapet. De Lannoy turning the cup slowly in his pale hands, eyes on the drill below, not on Nagoji. The sun low behind the far hills.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: When the fort burned at Colachel, I expected to die.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: What I did not expect was to be offered a choice.

panels.description: Lannoy, a soft laugh into his cup. Nagoji at his shoulder, watching him.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Serve Travancore, or rot in a cell until the company forgot my name.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: They would not have lifted a finger. I knew too much about their failures.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Dead men cannot testify.

panels.description: Full width. Lannoy turned to face Nagoji, the sunset behind him.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: The first time I put on Travancore colours, I felt as if I had swallowed broken glass.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: My mother would light candles for a son who had become, in their eyes, a traitor.

panels.description: Close on De Lannoy looking down at his own coat, thumbing the patch at the elbow: the same white cotton the king displayed, worn soft.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And now?

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Now it is cloth. It keeps the sun off my shoulders and the rain off my back.

panels.description: Low angle from the drill ground up at the parapet: De Lannoy in silhouette against the dusk sky, Nagoji a darker shape beside him, topknot against the light.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: The man inside has not changed. He has simply learned to wear a different skin.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's hand gripping the parapet stone: ridged fingernails, the old brand at the inner left wrist, bare forearm, the edge of his shoulder cloth. No coat sleeve.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You chose this. You accepted the king's offer.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did not choose to look like a Portuguese guard.

panels.description: Over De Lannoy's shoulder, looking down: the men below falling into formation in white mundu, no coats yet, their lines drawn like threads being pulled into a weave.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: No. But you chose to stay. To drill these men. To build these walls with me.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Each of those choices was a thread. The coat is simply the weaving.

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji leaning on the parapet, looking past the drill ground to the distant line of the sea, the colour going out of the sky. Not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: In Goa, there was an officer.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He was very particular about his cuffs.

panels.description: Full width. The stain takes the whole panel: a Goa corridor in grey dawn light, outside a cell door. The Goa officer: a pale European, clean-shaven pale jaw, hair tied in a queue under a black tricorne, a deep-cuffed white coat edged with gilt lace, a column of ornate gilt buttons, a red waistcoat beneath, a smallsword at his hip. The frame cuts off at his chin; his eyes are never shown. He draws one cuff straight with two fingers. Behind him, two Portuguese gaol guards waiting (dented steel morion helmets, loose off-white shirts, buff leather jerkins, dark breeches; nothing red or blue).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: He would come each morning, and check his cuffs before he gave orders.

panels.description: Tight on the officer's buckled shoe, an ornate silver buckle, lifting carefully over wet flagstones. The deep white cuff of his coat at the top of the frame. Whatever is on the floor stays out of frame.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: The coat was always clean. Even when there was blood on the floor.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: He would step around it, so as not to stain his shoes.

panels.description: From inside the cell, low, looking toward the door: the officer's white back leaving, the heavy door swinging shut behind him. At the top edge of the frame, a pair of empty iron manacles on a short chain hangs slack from a ring in the wall.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Then he would leave, and the guards would do what he had ordered.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And the coat would walk out as spotless as it had walked in.

panels.description: Back on the bastion at dusk. De Lannoy, quiet, turned toward Nagoji; Nagoji still looking at the sea (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat).

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: And when you see this coat...

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I see his cuffs. I see his shoes. I see the door closing behind him while I hung from the chains and wondered how many more mornings I could survive.

panels.description: Wide. Below, a drummer beating the evening call, men in white mundu forming up for the last drill of the day, no coats yet. The two men small at the parapet.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: I cannot make that memory disappear. No one can.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: But I can tell you what I have learned about clothes and men.

panels.description: Over their shoulders: De Lannoy moving to stand beside Nagoji, both looking down at the training ground, the last light long across it.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: In Zeeland, where I was born, there is a saying: the shirt does not make the sailor, but it tells you which ship he serves.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: I simply chose a different ship.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji turning his head toward him (topknot, silver chain of office, no coat).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if the ship is wrong?

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Then you are wrong with it. But you are wrong *together*.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: That is what the coat means. When you stand in a line with these men, you are telling the world: we fight as one.

panels.description: Tight on De Lannoy's pale hand setting his empty cup on the parapet stone; his face above it, turned to Nagoji.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: The Portuguese who tortured you were not evil because of their coats.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: They were evil because of what they chose to do while wearing them.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: You have the same choice.

panels.description: De Lannoy squared to face him, the last light on one side of his face, the drill ground dim behind.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: You can wear this cloth and be the man who trains cavalry to protect Padmini's fields.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Or you can refuse, and be the man who could not see past his scars to what his king was building.

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji's face in the last light, jaw set: not yet in uniform (topknot, silver chain of office, shoulder cloth, no coat).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words struck harder than I wanted to admit.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You make it sound simple.

panels.description: De Lannoy, rueful, less composed than we have seen him, looking down at his own frayed cuff. Nagoji beside him, not yet in uniform (topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, no coat).

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: It is not simple.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Some mornings I look at the coat on its peg and feel that glass in my throat again.

panels.description: Wide, looking down past the two men at the parapet: on the drill ground below, in the dim light, a young recruit (white mundu, no coat) has fumbled his musket drill; an officer shouts; the boy corrects himself. The first lamps being lit along the wall.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Then I put it on. And I go to the wall. And I do the work.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Eventually, the glass becomes smaller.

panels.description: Half the page. Nagoji's face in the last of the light, lamplight starting on one cheek: not yet in uniform (topknot, silver chain of office, shoulder cloth, no coat, no bandages, no knife). At the panel edge, one faint stain: Keshavrao's thin young face, black hair hacked short.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The coat was cloth. The man inside would still be me.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will wear it.

panels.description: De Lannoy nodding once. No smile, no hand on the shoulder. One soldier acknowledging another. Lamplight on the parapet.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: The first few days will be difficult. You will want to tear it off and burn it.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: I recommend against burning it. The quartermaster is very particular about inventory.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will try to restrain myself.

panels.description: Nagoji's quarters, small and bare. A small bronze mirror on the wall. Nagoji in the uniform for the first time: white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, knee breeches, buckled European riding boots, silver chain of office worn over the coat, topknot, no hat, no turban, no sash; clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, grey at the temples. No bandages, no knife. His reflection in the bronze is dimmer and warmer than the man.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The coats arrived a week later.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a long moment I was looking at a stranger.

panels.description: Tight on his hands drawing one white cuff straight with two fingers: a brown hand, ridged fingernails, plain brass buttons on the cuff. The gesture mirrors the Goa officer's in 11.1 exactly; the plain buttons and the brown hand are what differ.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The way that officer in Goa had done.

panels.description: The drill ground. Nagoji walking out in uniform, silver chain over the coat, talwar at his hip. His troop of Maravar riders, now in the same white coats, turning to stare; a few mutter behind their hands; one young horseman's laugh dying on his face as he meets Nagoji's eyes.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The same drills. Different cloth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Mount up.

panels.description: Full width. The troop swinging into their saddles as one, Nagoji already mounted at their head on Kayal, his white coat and silver chain bright against the red dust.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And we began.

panels.description: Wide. The parade ground, a squad of musketeers in the new white coats running drill. Through the gate rides a small embassy: three men in dark cloth, a secretary with a record book under his arm, and a thin figure in black on a mule under a broad travel hat. Nagoji in the foreground in uniform (white coat stiff across his shoulders, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, silver chain of office over the coat, topknot, no hat).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Portuguese came two weeks after the coats.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not with ships or guns. With letters and gifts, and a priest.

panels.description: Ramayyan appearing at Nagoji's elbow, already half turned toward the palace.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Viceroy sends his compliments. And his curiosity. Pepper, as always.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The Dutch came for pepper too. We know how that ended.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The king wants them to see our officers.

panels.description: Nagoji turning to follow, and stopping mid-turn. His face arrested.

Half the page. His point of view across the yard to the stables. The priest dismounting: older, grey hair under the hat, the scholar's stoop deeper, ink on his fingers, a plain black cassock with a small cross and no collar tab. His right hand has slipped inside his sleeve and is worrying at the cloth. He is talking to his secretary and has not seen Nagoji.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Father Duarte.

panels.description: Across the top, bleeding like a stain: a vaulted stone interrogation chamber lit red by a brazier, an empty stool in shadow. Duarte more than a decade younger, hair still dark with no grey, thin, a plain black cassock with a small cross and no collar tab, inclining his head in a small, weary nod.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: More than a decade since he had asked me whether I believed in God or only in powder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Since he had hesitated.

panels.description: Tight on Nagoji's buckled European riding boots crossing packed red earth, the hem of the white coat swinging above them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The kind that had clicked on the stone floors of Goa.

panels.description: Duarte turning. Three narrow vertical slices of his face across the panel: polite greeting, then confusion, then recognition. Production: generate each slice as its own frame and composite them into the strip, so the face stays the same man.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And then something I had not expected.

panels.description: Duarte, full face, afraid. His hands stay low; the right one twitches inside its sleeve.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: Senhor... I... that is...

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Father Duarte. You have come a long way from Goa.

panels.description: Full width. Over Duarte's shoulder: his eyes moving over Nagoji, the white coat and silver chain, the talwar at the hip, the drilling men behind him who would come if he raised a hand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He was calculating, as I had calculated once, the distance between himself and safety.

panels.description: Duarte, his voice catching. Behind him the secretary has stopped short, the record book clutched to his chest.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: You survived. The ship... we heard it was lost in a storm.

panels.description: Over Duarte's grey head and black shoulder onto Nagoji in uniform, level, the silver chain over the white coat.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Most of it was.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did not.

panels.description: Duarte's hand rising toward the cross at his throat, then stopping short, as if the gesture would be inadequate.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: I have thought of you. Over the years. I have wondered...

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Whether I would come for you?

panels.description: Low angle on Duarte, steadier, his hand gone back inside his sleeve and working at the cloth.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: Whether you found what you were fighting for.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: That night, in the chamber, you said God favours whoever has the better powder.

panels.description: Full width. Duarte's gaze across the parade ground: the white-coated lines, the star-fort walls, a field gun on its carriage.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: It seems you found the better powder.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I found something. Whether it is what I was fighting for, I am still deciding.

panels.description: Wide. The two men small in the middle of the fort's business: horses led to water, an officer shouting commands, the secretary hovering at a distance, unsure whether to intervene.
Nagoji close to him, quiet.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I could have you arrested.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Some of these men lost brothers in your dungeons. Some of them lost more.

panels.description: Duarte, jaw tight. He does not look away.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: You could. It would not be unjust.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: No. It would not.

panels.description: Narrow strip. Both faces, neither speaking.
Tight on Nagoji alone, Duarte out of frame.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But I am not going to.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Do you know why?

panels.description: Duarte's small shake of the head in the foreground, the back of his grey head and black shoulder; Nagoji beyond him, in uniform, answering.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Because you hesitated.

panels.description: Stain. A red-lit stone chamber. João's thick ruddy wrist in a rolled cream shirt sleeve under a brown leather jerkin, reaching toward a glowing brazier; Duarte's thin ink-stained hand, more than a decade younger, shooting out of a plain black cassock sleeve and gripping it. Only one cassock sleeve in the frame.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: In the chamber, when João reached for the brazier, you stopped him.

panels.description: Stain. A Goa courtyard of whitewashed walls under glaring sun. Duarte more than a decade younger, hair still dark, in a broad round travel hat and a plain black cassock, making a slow, deliberate sign of the cross toward a chain of prisoners in grey, brown and ochre captivity rags. Portuguese musketeers in broad hats and buff leather coats along the wall, nothing red or blue.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: At the gate, you made the sign of the cross. Not the quick one, the one that wards off evil.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: The slow one. The one that asks for something.

panels.description: Duarte's eyes glistening. He blinks it away.
Duarte.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: I asked for your forgiveness.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: I have asked for it every day since.

panels.description: Nagoji in uniform. Behind him, a faint stain: a thin young hand slipping from a rope in black storm water.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I cannot give you that. What was done to me is not mine alone to forgive.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Keshavrao drowned in that storm. Others died in your cells. Their forgiveness is not mine to grant.

panels.description: Nagoji stepping closer, the silver chain and plain brass buttons of the coat catching the light.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I wear this coat now. I drill these men.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The man you tortured is gone.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The man who stands here now has made his choices. Some of them haunt me. Some of them I am proud of. Most are somewhere in between.

panels.description: Duarte nodding slowly.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: Then we are alike in that. More than I would have thought.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Perhaps.

panels.description: Two-shot, face to face, an arm's length apart. Nagoji holds Duarte's eyes.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: When you return to Goa, tell them what you saw here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Tell them that the man they branded as property now commands the cavalry that guards this coast.

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji walking away across the parade ground in his white coat, his back to Duarte, toward the drilling lines. Small behind him, the secretary hurrying to Duarte's side.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The glass in my throat, the one Lannoy had spoken of, was still there.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: But it was smaller.

panels.description: Wide. The drill ground in morning light. At its edge, the Prince, about fourteen: tall enough to look Nagoji in the chest, narrow in the shoulders, beardless, his uncle's sharp cheekbones and his mother's watchful eyes, in a plain training tunic with no silks or jewels. Two Nair guards a pace behind him, hands near their hilts. Nagoji facing him in uniform (white coat, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, silver chain of office over the coat, topknot; no bandages, no knife).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three months after the coats.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: My uncle says I am to learn from you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Learn what?

panels.description: Tight on the Prince. No self-pity. A flat statement of fact.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: How to stay alive when men want me dead.

panels.description: Inset, bleeding like a stain, in daylight: the great temple, its carved gopuram behind. The heir at ten, small, in white, frozen, eyes wide. A curved knife flashing down in a hand whose owner is out of frame. Between blade and boy, a man's shoulder in white silk turning in to take it. No blood. No face but the boy's. No priest.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The King's blood on white silk.

panels.description: Two-shot, the Prince squared up to Nagoji.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Your uncle could have sent you to De Lannoy.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: De Lannoy teaches formations. My uncle says you teach survival.

panels.description: Nagoji looking past the Prince at the guards.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They stay at the gate. On the training ground, you are not a prince. You are a student.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If I strike you, they do not interfere. If you fall, they do not help you rise.

panels.description: The older guard, grey at his temples, stepping forward.

copy.speaker: OLD GUARD
copy.text: Highness, the Maharaja's orders were...

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: To learn from this man. I cannot learn if I am wrapped in silk. Go.

panels.description: The guards walking away toward the gate. The Prince turning back to Nagoji, the set of his jaw exactly his uncle's.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: What first?

panels.description: Nagoji, in uniform, tossing a wooden practice sword at the Prince's chest. The Prince catches it, barely.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: First, you learn how much you do not know.

panels.description: Wide, a strip of three beats in one panel: the Prince's legs swept from under him; the Prince disarmed, his wooden sword spinning away; the Prince at dusk bowing to Nagoji, a fresh bruise on his forearm over a fading one. Production: generate each beat as its own frame and composite them into the strip, so the boy stays the same boy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He did not once ask to rest.

panels.description: Full width. The Prince taking a fall, rolling, and coming up with his sword ready. At Nagoji's shoulder, Ramayyan has appeared without a sound.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You are trying to kill the heir.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am trying to make him harder to kill. There is a difference.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Senior Rani has concerns.

panels.description: The Prince mid-drill, his eyes flicking sideways and holding a heartbeat too long. Nagoji (in uniform) follows the look: in the shade of the armoury wall stands the Senior Rani of Attingal, in white without ornament, her hair pulled back severely, her face unreadable.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Continue. A king who is distracted by his mother will be distracted by everything.

panels.description: An hour later, the sun higher, dust hanging. Nagoji walking to her. Behind him, the Prince drinking deep from a water skin, his tunic dark with sweat.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Highness. You could have summoned me to the palace.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: I wished to see. There is a difference between reports and observation.

panels.description: Her eyes on her son.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: He has changed. The way he stands. Even the servants have noticed. And the cost?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Bruises. A few cuts that will scar. Nothing that will not heal.

panels.description: She turns to face him fully. Her voice drops.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: When he was born, my brother held him and wept.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: I have spent fourteen years keeping him alive. Tasters, guards, astrologers.

panels.description: Full width. Her face, hard.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: Now I send him to you because all my counting has made him soft.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: At the temple, he stood like a deer in torchlight.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He will not freeze again. I am burning that out of him.

panels.description: The Senior Rani, the faintest ghost of a smile.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: I know. That is why I have not stopped you.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: A mother's fear can become a son's chains.

panels.description: She presses something into his hand. Inset, tight: a small gold coin, old, worn smooth by generations of fingers, in Nagoji's open left hand: ridged fingernails, a thin pale healed scar across the palm, the white cuff and a plain brass button of his coat at the wrist.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: This was my grandmother's. It passes from woman to woman in this house.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then why give it to me?

panels.description: She takes the coin back.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: I am not giving it to you. I am showing it to you.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: So that you understand what you are training. Not a soldier. Not a prince. A line.

panels.description: Close on her face, perfectly calm.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: If you break him, I will have you killed. Slowly. With full knowledge of what is happening to you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I understand, Highness.

copy.speaker: SENIOR RANI
copy.text: He says you tell him unpleasant truths. Continue.

panels.description: Full width. She walks away, back straight, steps measured. The Prince has come to Nagoji's elbow; both watch her go.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: She likes you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: She threatened to have me killed slowly.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: Yes. That is how you know. The ones she does not like, she simply has killed. Without warning.

panels.description: Wide. Before dawn, the training ground empty and misted. Two small riders walking their horses in slow circles: Nagoji in uniform on Kayal, the Prince on a smaller grey.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The second month.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: In the Deccan, a man's horse is his second self.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: Our kings ride elephants.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Elephants are for show. A horse can take you where elephants cannot. Away from danger, when danger is the only certainty.

panels.description: Trotting side by side, the sun clearing the tree line, the world gone gold and green. The Prince looking straight ahead, not at Nagoji.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: Pillai. At the temple, when the chaver came, I froze.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: I saw the blade and I could not move. If my uncle had not...

panels.description: Both reined in, the horses facing each other.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He did. That is what matters.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You were ten years old. A boy can be forgiven.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: I am not ten now.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji, level, the low sun behind him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If it happens again, your body will know what to do before your mind has time to be afraid.

copy.speaker: PRINCE (off)
copy.text: And if instinct is not enough?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then you die. But you die moving, not standing still.

panels.description: Full width. The Prince looking at him for a long moment, the two horses standing in the gold light.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: You do not speak to me like the others do.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: The others speak around the truth. You speak through it.

panels.description: Wide. The drill ground. In the foreground, a Nair captain (older, heavier, ash stripes on his forehead) muttering to Nagoji (in uniform, silver chain over the coat, no forehead mark). Behind them, the Prince in the same white coat as the others, visibly the youngest and slightest man on the ground, beardless and narrow-shouldered, hauling a collapsed recruit into the shade and holding his own water skin to the man's lips.

copy.speaker: NAIR CAPTAIN
copy.text: The heir cannot be treated like a common soldier.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That is the point.

panels.description: Evening on the bastion. The Prince, in his white coat, beside Nagoji at the parapet.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: The men look at me differently now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They look at you as one of them. Is that not what you wanted?

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: I do not know what I wanted.

panels.description: Close on the Prince, looking out over the training ground, not at Nagoji.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: I only knew I did not want to be the boy at the temple again. The one who stood there while others bled for him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: You will never be that boy again. You have made certain of it.

panels.description: Two-shot. The Prince rolling his shoulders the way he has been taught, then a small, wry smile.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: Thank you, Pillai. For not treating me like glass.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Glass breaks. You are iron that has not yet been forged. The fire is uncomfortable. But it is necessary.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: Then I will try to enjoy the burning.

panels.description: Full width. The Prince walking down from the bastion, past guards who no longer hover so close, past men who nod to him as a fellow soldier instead of bowing. Nagoji watching from above. At the panel edge, a faint stain: a ten-year-old boy in white standing in the courtyard of a Kerala house, wide-eyed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That boy was gone.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In his place walked someone who might, one day, be worthy of the throne his uncle was building for him.

panels.description: The artillery yard. Thoma Ittyerah (broad, a white tunic, betel-stained teeth) crossing himself, one palm about to rest on the barrel of a bronze field gun. His mixed crew of Syrian Christians and Nairs waiting. Nagoji watching, in uniform.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The artillery came under new command that season. Thoma Ittyerah.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His people had been Christians on this coast long before any Portuguese ship troubled these waters.

panels.description: Thoma, a big hand flat on the gun.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: My grandfather cast cannon for the Zamorin. My father cast them for Kochi. I cast them for Travancore.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: The metal does not care which king pays for the mould.

panels.description: Thoma squinting along the barrel, adjusting the elevation.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You do not pray to the same gods as your men.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: No. But we bleed the same colour. That is enough for a gun crew.

panels.description: Wide. The gun fires. Downrange, a wooden target bursts into splinters. The crew in fixed places around the gun, loader, rammer, the man with the slow match, each moving in exact ritual order.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Their faith was not in any god, but in the mathematics of fire.

panels.description: In the drifting smoke, Thoma grinning through it, teeth stained dark red-brown with betel. Nagoji beside him in his white coat.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: The Dutch and the Portuguese think history began when their ships arrived.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: This coast has buried empires before them. It will bury more.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And yet we wear their coats now. And fire their cannons.

panels.description: Close on Thoma as the smoke thins, unbothered, wiping his hands.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: We wear what is useful. We fire what works.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: That is not surrender. That is wisdom.

panels.description: Wide. A river dock, a small boat pulled in beside stacked barrels of saltpetre. Avraham ben Ephraim just stepped off: dark coat despite the heat, a cap, a beard that falls to his chest. Thoma's hand on Avraham's shoulder, presenting him. Avraham giving Nagoji's white coat a slow once-over; Nagoji answering with a half bow.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: Avraham ben Ephraim. His family has traded with mine for four generations.

copy.speaker: AVRAHAM
copy.text: The man who teaches horses to dance with muskets.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The man who tries.

panels.description: Thoma laughing, a hand on a barrel. Avraham unsmiling but not displeased.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: The Jews of Kochi have a saying.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: The Portuguese came and went, the Dutch came and are going, the English are coming. We remain.

panels.description: Another evening. Lamplight. Avraham and Thoma over cups of arrack, account books and manifests spread between them. Nagoji with them, his coat unbuttoned.

copy.speaker: AVRAHAM
copy.text: I doubt all kings. But this king pays his debts. That is worth something.

copy.speaker: AVRAHAM
copy.text: We have outlasted Pharaohs and Caesars and Inquisitors. We will outlast kings of pepper, too.

panels.description: Full width. Avraham's small boat going out into the dusk. Lamps being lit along the fort walls. Nagoji and Thoma small on the wall, watching it go.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Strange allies, these.

copy.speaker: THOMA
copy.text: All allies are strange. Until you need them.

panels.description: Evening in the fort's small armoury, the last daylight slanting through the open door, a lamp already lit on the racks of spears and a new shipment of blades. De Lannoy lifting a talwar, feeling its weight. Nagoji beside him in uniform.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Your swords are better for cutting from horseback. Our straight blades are better for thrusts on foot.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We make do with what the land asks. If the ground is cluttered, curve your steel.

panels.description: Tight: De Lannoy has flipped the sword and offers it hilt first. Nagoji's brown hand, ridged fingernails, plain brass buttons at the white cuff, closing on the hilt; De Lannoy's pale freckled hand, from a frayed and much-mended cuff, still on the flat of the blade.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: If we are to be blamed together, we may as well be armed together.

panels.description: De Lannoy leaning against a rack of spears, staring at some point between them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have accepted that you will never go back.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Back where? To ships that would call me traitor? To a land that has already written my name in a different set of books?

panels.description: De Lannoy straightening, looking out through the armoury door at the men drilling in the yard.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: This is my fort now. These are my men.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: If I spend the rest of my life making sure they do not die as stupidly as some of my countrymen did, perhaps that will be enough to balance a few lines.

panels.description: Full width. De Lannoy turned back to Nagoji, the lamp throwing his long shadow across the racks.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Under whose standard do we truly stand, Ananthan Pillai?

panels.description: Two men in the lamplight, the talwar in Nagoji's hand.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: The king's? The idea of this place? The memory of the men who died at Colachel?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: All of them. On different days.

panels.description: De Lannoy nodding, and then, at Nagoji's answer, smiling.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: On the days when it is the king's, we must be careful. Kings change. Places endure longer.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have been talking to Revathi.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: She scolds me too. Apparently my foreignness does not exempt me.

panels.description: Wide. The two men stepping out onto the wall: De Lannoy taller, bare-headed, pale hair; Nagoji darker, black topknot, silver chain catching the light over his white coat. Below, under the foreigner's tooth, men still drilling in the waning light: Maravar horse and Nair musketeers alike in white coats, Thoma's gun crew at their piece.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two men far from the places that had birthed us, bound to a banner that was neither of our first choosing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Whatever names future scribes gave this army, for this moment, it was ours.

panels.description: Half the page, final. No figures. The banner staff from below, filling the frame against the last of the light: at the top, the royal standard, red with a silver conch; below it, a smaller pennant, white with a dark blue diagonal line crossed by a dark blue curved line. Both lifting in the evening wind.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We stood under its standard.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Together.
